newsitem.title: FRANCE: SUEZ, LYONNAISE CLINCH MERGER DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SUEZ, LYONNAISE CLINCH MERGER DEAL.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez on Friday agreed a merger deal, which would create a strong European utilities group, Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet told reporters.
The merger will take the form of a swap of 20 Lyonnaise shares for 41 Suez shares.
The new Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux group sees a return on invested capital of at least 10 percent, Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod told journalists.
In a statement, the company said it expected a 1997 net profit of at least 3.5 billion francs ($604.5 million).
The company said it aimed to double its earnings per share in five years' after 1997.
"For the 1997 year, the outlook for the net profit for Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux is for a figure of over 3.5 billion francs," the statement said.
"Beyond this year (1997) the objective is to double the net earnings per share in five years," the joint statement said.
Through the merger, the shareholders of the new group will benefit from an immediate positive effect on net earnings per share of eight percent on the 1997 results, it said.
The company will have a solid financial structure with a gearing of net debt to shareholders funds of 46 percent.
The shareholders will benefit from "an improvement in the quality of results in terms of visibility and recurring profits," the statement said.
